name: Alexander Hamilton U.S. Custom House

dates.altered: The Customs Service left in 1971; restored and rehabilitated after a 1978 competition, and the George Gustav Heye Center of the National Museum of the American Indian opened in it in 1994.
dates.note: Wikipedia's infobox says 'Built 1901-1907' and its text 'erected from 1902 to 1907'; the General Services Administration, which owns the building, prints 'Construction Dates: 1900-1907' and a timeline reading '1899: Cass Gilbert wins design competition ... 1900-1907: The U.S. Custom House is constructed.' Three start years across two sources; none is edited.

refs.title: Alexander Hamilton U.S. Custom House, New York, NY - U.S. General Services Administration
refs.note: The owner. Its building-facts block gives 'Architectural Style: Beaux Arts', 'Architect: Cass Gilbert', 'Primary Materials: Granite Exterior Marble interior' and the GSA building number NY0131ZZ, and names Daniel Chester French's Four Continents at the base. It describes the building as 'a steel-framed, seven-story structure on the south side of Bowling Green at the foot of Broadway' deliberately facing the green rather than the harbour.

note: Written for WP-11.2 Tranche 2 as an addition to beaux-arts-american. Chosen as the documentary case because its owner is a federal agency that publishes the construction dates, materials, authorship and storey count on a stable page, so the record can be cited rather than characterised - and because the three start years the two sources give between them are exactly the sort of small disagreement an exemplar with no locator used to hide.
